_note: Hand-authored real-world resource episodes — external domain knowledge, NOT derived from the database. Dates are APPROXIMATE (month-level). Each entry MUST carry a one-sentence justification. `episodes` are TIGHTENING periods (label=1); `negative_periods` are explicit NON-tightening / oversupply periods (label=0) so the classifier learns both classes. NAND now appears in BOTH: its 2023 glut is a clean negative, and its late-2024→2025 supply-cut + enterprise/AI-SSD recovery is a (supply-discipline-driven) tightening — the justification notes that driver honestly.
_lead_weeks_reasoning: Public signals (news, filings) typically precede visible price tightening by ~1-2 months; 8 weeks of pre-start labeling captures that lead-in. Applies to `episodes` (tightening) only — negative_periods are labeled exactly over their stated window with no lead.

episodes.justification: Server/DDR5 DRAM contract prices rose sharply through 2024-2025 as memory makers diverted wafer capacity toward HBM for AI datacenters, tightening conventional DRAM supply.
HBM3/HBM3E was effectively sold out through 2024 into 2025 as AI-accelerator demand outran the combined HBM capacity of SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron.
Demand for H100-class AI GPUs vastly exceeded supply constrained by TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging and HBM availability, forcing multi-quarter customer allocation from 2023 onward.

NAND flash contract prices recovered sharply from late 2024 into 2025 as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron held deep wafer-output cuts while enterprise/AI-server SSD demand rose, tightening NAND supply after the 2023 glut (driven by supply discipline plus AI-SSD demand, not pure AI-demand pull like HBM/GPU).

negative_periods.justification: Through most of 2023 DRAM was in severe oversupply with weak PC/smartphone demand and bloated inventories, driving contract prices down for consecutive quarters — a clearly NON-tightening (loosening) period before the 2024 AI-driven reversal.
NAND flash was in a deep glut through 2023 with double-digit quarterly price declines that forced industry-wide production cuts — an unambiguously non-tightening period.
